People Surge, a national alliance of disaster survivors, and PISTON, a federation of Filipino drivers and operators, staged a protest at a Petron station in Pasig City over rising fuel prices. Protesters pelted posters with black clay and defaced signage to dramatize public frustration, demanding the suspension of VAT and excise taxes, repeal of the Oil Deregulation Law, and accountability for oil companies profiting from the energy crisis, with prices expected to reach P80 per liter and possibly P100.

The protest echoes recent European activism where demonstrators targeted the Mona Lisa at the Louvre, throwing soup to highlight systemic failures in food security and rising living costs. Both actions used bold, symbolic tactics to draw attention to grievances and press authorities for solutions, demonstrating a pattern of public frustration against perceived exploitation and economic pressure.

People Surge emphasized support for drivers, farmers, and fisherfolk facing the burden of higher fuel costs. The Department of Energy said it is coordinating with oil companies to maintain discounted rates for public utility vehicles, drivers, and delivery services.

WTA Miami

 Katerina Siniakova vs Camila Osorio

🧠 Form & Context

🇨🇿 Katerina Siniakova (#42, right-handed, 174 cm)
📈 2026: 7–6 overall | 7–6 on hard
✅ Indian Wells: beat Kenin, Fernandez, and Andreeva before retiring against Svitolina in the last 16
🔁 Dangerous returner with a very live baseline game, but the recent Indian Wells retirement is the main red flag here
💥 Already faced Osorio in Doha this year and pushed that matchup deep, so there is recent tactical reference on both sides

🇨🇴 Camila Osorio (#58, right-handed, 162 cm)
📈 2026: 12–6 overall | 12–6 on hard
✅ Won the Manila title, then reached the third round in Indian Wells with wins over Stephens and Jovic
🔁 Comes in with better hard-court volume this season and already owns a 2026 win over Siniakova in Doha
⚠️ Can be very competitive from the baseline, but her second-serve vulnerability remains the pressure point in tighter matches

🔍 Match Breakdown
This is a very interesting first-round matchup because both players bring competitive hard-court form, but the paths to winning look different.

Siniakova has the stronger return profile and the more disruptive all-court skill set. She is not a huge server, yet she compensates with compact returning, good timing off both wings, and the ability to redirect pace. In a match built around pressure on second serve and extended baseline exchanges, that gives her a real edge. Her Indian Wells run also showed strong resilience, especially in comeback wins over Fernandez and Andreeva.

Osorio, though, is very live here. She already beat Siniakova in Doha in three sets, and her 12–6 hard-court start to the season is the stronger raw record. She is the steadier rhythm player when rallies settle, and when she gets time to build points with her forehand patterns, she can drag opponents into uncomfortable physical exchanges. Her recent title run in Manila also suggests confidence is in a healthier place than her ranking alone might indicate.

The key hinge is serve quality under pressure. Siniakova’s return game should create more break chances, while Osorio may need to protect her second serve better than she typically does. The other issue is physical trust: Siniakova’s retirement in Indian Wells cannot be ignored, especially in a potentially long three-set battle.

Miami Gardens is also forecast to be cool and showery around match time, which points to slightly heavier conditions than a clean fast-court script and should help returners stay involved in rallies. That leans a little toward the player who can win with pressure, variation, and repeat return depth rather than free points alone.

🔮 Prediction
This feels close, and the odds reflect that correctly. Osorio has the fresher 2026 hard record and already owns one win in the matchup this season, but Siniakova still looks like the more dangerous problem-solver in a tactical, pressure-heavy contest.

If Siniakova is physically fine, her return game and ability to disrupt rhythm should give her the upper hand. If her level dips physically or the match turns into a long grind with repeated service pressure, Osorio has a real upset path.

Prediction: Siniakova

The @MMDA  inaugurates on Tuesday (March 17, 2026) bike-to-work end-of-trip facilities at the Motorcycle Riding Academy in Pasig City in line with its commitment to promote active and sustainable mobility in Metro Manila.

The newly opened facilities include four shower rooms, ensuring a comfortable, inclusive, and accessible experience for cyclists. They also feature secure bike racks and changing spaces, supporting daily commuters who use bicycles for work. | MMDA photos
